source_refs.note: Homeotherms: a main subheading of 13.3.2 Types of Animals on the basis ability of Thermoregulation, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 8-8.

blocks.text: These animals maintain relatively constant internal body temperatures, regardless of environmental fluctuations. They use "thermostats" (hypothalamus in the brain) to trigger cooling or heating responses. Examples include mammals and birds. For instance, humans maintain their internal temperature at roughly 37°C whether they are in very cold or very hot environments.
